Question:
In \(\triangle ABC,\) a point \(E\) is on \(\overline{AB}\) with \(AE=1\) and \(EB=2.\) Point \(D\) is on \(\overline{AC}\) so that \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}\) and point \(F\) is on \(\overline{BC}\) so that \(\overline{EF} \parallel \overline{AC}.\) What is the ratio of the area of \(CDEF\) to the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2018_AMC_8_Q20_question_fig1.svg)
Solution:
The parallel lines make two smaller triangles similar to the whole triangle. Since \(AE=1\) and \(EB=2\), the full side \(AB\) is \(3\).

For \(\triangle AED\), the length ratio to \(\triangle ABC\) is \(AE/AB=1/3\), because \(DE\parallel BC\). Its area is therefore \((1/3)^2=1/9\) of the whole.

For \(\triangle EBF\), the length ratio is \(EB/AB=2/3\), because \(EF\parallel AC\). Its area is \((2/3)^2=4/9\) of the whole. Similar-triangle areas use squared length ratios because both base and height scale.

These two triangles and quadrilateral \(CDEF\) partition \(ABC\). The quadrilateral's fraction is

\[
1-\frac19-\frac49=\boxed{\frac49},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
